raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. Its architecture comprises three layers: an Observe layer with lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns, an Intelligence Layer that acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, task value, and "drift," and an Execution Layer, an "Agent Factory" that automates the generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. The system leverages existing foundation models, focusing on understanding the "Work Graph" to identify resource inefficiencies and areas where AI can assist.

raw.one_liner: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" that enables AI-first companies to visualize, validate, and implement AI automation at scale by analyzing work patterns and generating AI agents.
raw.thesis: Narma is creating an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an Observe layer to capture work patterns, an Intelligence Layer to detect employee intent and task value, and an Execution Layer (Agent Factory) that generates and deploys AI agents for high-ROI automation. This system focuses on analyzing the "Work Graph" to identify inefficiencies and opportunities for AI intervention, rather than developing new foundation models. It aims to solve the problem of enterprises lacking telemetry for AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and system/human resource drift by providing a comprehensive solution for seeing, proving, and deploying AI automation at scale. The founder appears to be building a growth-oriented startup, given the focus on "at scale" deployment for enterprises. The venture is currently at the idea stage, as evidenced by the detailed description of the concept without mention of a working product or users. Narma positions itself as a complement to existing foundation models, leveraging them to create an overarching intelligence and execution layer for AI automation within enterprises. It's not replacing existing AI models but rather orchestrating their application for maximum business value.
raw.what_makes_this_different: Narma's unique contribution is its "Enterprise Agentic Brain" architecture that provides a full-stack solution for AI automation, from observation to intelligent analysis and autonomous agent deployment, without building its own foundational AI models. It focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify specific, high-ROI opportunities for AI intervention.
